title: Gemini API Pricing 2026: Every Model, Tokens & Limits
summary: Gemini API pricing structures determine your monthly expenses based on token usage and model selection.
body_markdown:
## Compare Gemini 3.1 Pro input costs


Gemini 1.5 Pro had a base input cost of $1.25 per 1M tokens, which made it a price-disruptor at the time compared with the premium charged by legacy flagship models.


$1.25 per 1M tokens was exactly half the $2.50 per 1M tokens charged for GPT-4o. This rate, verified by[Compute Comparison](https://computecomparison.com/llm-model/gemini-1-5-pro) , meant you could double your prompt volume for the same capital outlay.


When compared to[Claude](https://claude.com/pricing) 3.5 Sonnet, which carried a $3.00 per 1M token price tag according to Compute Comparison, Gemini 1.5 Pro had a **58% discount** .


### Gemini 3.1 Pro vs. GPT-6 Astra for reasoning tasks


Gemini 1.5 Pro undercut GPT-4o by 50% on input costs at the time, meaning companies could process twice the amount of information for the same budget.


While GPT-4o remained a standard for many enterprise integrations at the time, its $2.50 per 1M tokens cost meant that high-reasoning workloads scaled poorly compared to the $1.25 cost of Gemini 1.5 Pro.


If you're building long-horizon agents, this price gap determines whether a feature is a profitable product or a subsidized experiment.


### Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite pricing for high-frequency tasks


Gemini 1.5 Flash had the absolute lowest entry point for high-volume automation at the time, yet you must account for four hidden billing drivers:


- Grounding fees ($14/1k searches after 5k free)
- Image/Video tokenization overhead
- Context caching storage fees ($0.01/GB/hour)
- Multi-modal input rounding


The "sticker price" is rarely the final cost, so you must calculate storage duration for cached prompts to avoid surprise line items.


### Price-to-performance benchmarks for 2026 models


The current landscape for 2026 models reflects a stratified market where Gemini 3.1 Pro and Gemini 3.8 Flash compete against specialized offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI.


Claude Fable 5.1, designed by[Anthropic](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/about-claude/models/overview) for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, targets the high-end tier.


Claude Haiku 5.5, the[Anthropic](https://docs.claude.com/) model for high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks like classification and routing, competes directly with the Gemini Flash-Lite series on speed.


GPT-6 Astra, the flagship from OpenAI, maintains a premium pricing structure for complex reasoning and coding.


Gemini 3.1 Pro remains the economic leader for standard context. Specialized tasks like agentic coding or real-time routing require you to choose models based on their specific architectural strengths.
